Wider Sports News.title: How Goalhanger built a podcasting empire and why it’s investing in the next one
Wider Sports News.summary: Goalhanger CFO Andy Hodgson explains why the company behind The Rest Is Football is now taking equity in emerging brands in exchange for advertising opportunities. The post How Goalhanger built a podcasting empire and why it’s investing in the next one appeared first on SportsPro .
Wider Sports News.body:
When Gary Lineker departed the BBC last year, he had the enviable safety net of co-owning a company named by The Times as Britain’s fastest growing company in 2025. Co-founded in 2018 by Gary Lineker, Goalhanger produces some of the world’s popular podcasts, including The Rest is Football, The Rest is Politics and The Rest is History.

Over the past three years, annual revenues have risen by 321 per cent to UK£37.5 million (US$50.4 million) and Goalhanger now counts US firm The Chernin Group as a minority shareholder.

Wider Sports News.title: ESPN to bid for 2030 World Cup rights in the US as Fifa eyes up to US$2bn
Wider Sports News.summary: Fox’s ratings and commercial success is attracting streamers for the 2030 and 2034 World Cups as Fifa looks set for big payday. The post ESPN to bid for 2030 World Cup rights in the US as Fifa eyes up to US$2bn appeared first on SportsPro .
Wider Sports News.body:
ESPN chairman Jimmy Pitaro has confirmed the pay-TV sports network will bid for the US broadcast rights to the next Fifa World Cup. The 2026 Fifa World Cup held in North America has been a huge success for Fox, which has enjoyed huge ratings and significant demand from advertisers. Fox and Telemundo, which owns the Spanish language rights, are anticipating US$850 million in advertising revenue.

Fifa hopes this growth will attract multiple bidders and allow it to demand a significant premium on the $485 million Fox currently pays – a sum many believe is below market value.

Wider Sports News.title: Fans now discover clubs through players, content and culture
Wider Sports News.summary: The path to football fandom has changed, with players, stories and culture often reaching fans before the badge. The post Fans now discover clubs through players, content and culture appeared first on SportsPro .
Wider Sports News.body:
Football fandom increasingly starts in the wrong order. Someone sees a player on TikTok, watches a few clips and follows the account. A few months later they know the starting XI and are wondering whether £95 for the new away shirt is actually quite reasonable.

The badge arrived somewhere in the middle. That matters because clubs have traditionally thought about fandom as something rooted in place and inherited over time. The Rise of the ‘Second Club Fan’: How rights holders can understand, win and monetise multi-club fandom, new research from MTM and Engage Digital Partners, shows a broader picture. Fans now encounter clubs through individual players and wider culture, with digital platforms creating routes into fandom that barely existed a generation ago.

Wider Sports News.title: World Cup paradox: Why sport thrives in an age of cultural fragmentation
Wider Sports News.summary: As media and entertainment fragment into localised niches, global sport thrives by uniting diverse identities without erasing cultural differences. The post World Cup paradox: Why sport thrives in an age of cultural fragmentation appeared first on SportsPro .
Wider Sports News.body:
In its June 13–19 edition, The Economist published an article titled “A World Cup Paradox.” Despite the sport-centric headline, the article wasn’t really about soccer but more about media and culture.

For much of the 20th century, American entertainment enjoyed unparalleled global influence. Hollywood studios, television networks and record labels produced cultural products consumed around the world. Whether one lived in Brisbane, Berlin, Buenos Aires or Bangkok, there was a good chance people were watching, listening or discussing the same movies, music or TV shows.

Wider Sports News.title: From Hungary to home plate: How smarter ticket pricing unlocks double-digit growth for minor league and niche sports properties
Wider Sports News.summary: DynamO Pricing built its dynamic pricing platform in Budapest. Six years on, it is pricing tickets for a dozen American baseball clubs, the West End, multiple motorsport properties and the Edinburgh International Festival. The post From Hungary to home plate: How smarter ticket pricing unlocks double-digit growth for minor league and niche sports properties appeared first on SportsPro .
Wider Sports News.body:
DynamO Pricing was founded in Budapest in 2017 and launched its proprietary dynamic pricing platform in 2020. Today, the company has roughly 100 active clients across Europe and the US, integrations with platforms including Spektrix and Tickets.com, and a footprint spanning Hungarian arts venues, London’s West End, the Edinburgh International Festival, a global open‑wheel motorsport championship and, this season, at least 12 professional baseball clubs.

SportsPro spoke with Attila Gazdag, the company’s board member and chief revenue officer, about the journey so far and where DynamO Pricing goes next. What are your views on the commercial landscape in sport right now, and what does that mean for a company like yours?

Wider Sports News.title: Aston Villa sign ‘UK£20m-a-year’ Visit Rwanda shirt sponsorship despite sportswashing concerns
Wider Sports News.summary: Villa sign controversial deal as betting sponsor ban and new financial rules come into force. The post Aston Villa sign ‘UK£20m-a-year’ Visit Rwanda shirt sponsorship despite sportswashing concerns appeared first on SportsPro .
Wider Sports News.body:
Aston Villa have signed up Visit Rwanda as their new main sponsor, with the partnership considered the most lucrative deal in the club’s history. Visit Rwanda’s branding will appear on the front of all men’s, women’s, and academy teams’ shirts as part of the deal. The east African country’s tourism board will replace Betano, which had been Villa’s principal partner since 2024 as part of a reported UK£40 million (US$53.5 million) deal.

According to The Athletic, the new deal is worth up to UK£20 million (US$26.7 million) each year if bonuses are met. “This is a very exciting partnership for Aston Villa Football Club and a symbol of the club’s continuing expansion and growth into international markets,” said Francesco Calvo, Aston Villa president of business operations.

Wider Sports News.title: Why Athvance Capital is looking beyond sport’s trophy assets
Wider Sports News.summary: Danny Menken, co-founder of Athvance Capital, explains why sport’s next value opportunity sits beyond elite rights holders, how evergreen capital aligns with founders, and why US institutions are backing Europe’s operator-led growth story. The post Why Athvance Capital is looking beyond sport’s trophy assets appeared first on SportsPro .
Wider Sports News.body:
Europe’s sports landscape is fragmented across multiple federations and rights structures, which is enough to deter most generalist capital. However, Athvance Capital sees that complexity as its edge, and has spent its first year building a portfolio spanning multi-club football, combat sports, padel and beach volleyball and the infrastructure that holds them up.

Launched in January this year, Athvance Capital is a European sports investment fund founded by Danny Menken, the former Eurosport managing director and Eleven Sports co-founder, with ex-JP Morgan investment banker Karim Ben Rejeb.

How Does the HSBC Partnership Support ClearScore? The ClearScore growth strategy receives a significant boost through this renewed collaboration with HSBC Innovation Banking. By providing a Senior Term Loan alongside a Revolving Credit Facility, HSBC offers the flexible capital structure necessary for a high-growth fintech to scale its operations. This financing allows ClearScore to invest in product innovation efforts and market expansion without diluting equity.

Rugby.title: 'There were questions about who we are and whether we deserve to be here'
Rugby.summary: Hong Kong China hailed the biggest result in the nation's rugby history after an astonishing 42-40 comeback victory over Uruguay in Montevideo...
Rugby.body:
Hong Kong China hailed the biggest result in the nation’s rugby history after an astonishing 42-40 comeback victory over Uruguay in Montevideo, a win that secured their first-ever World Rugby Nations Cup triumph and saw them defeat the world No.17 side on home soil.

Having trailed 26-13 at half-time and 33-20 early in the second half, Hong Kong produced a stunning fightback before Paul Altier landed an 81st-minute penalty to snatch victory.

Rugby.title: The 'part' that Gregor Townsend has 'been most impressed with and pleased' with Scotland
Rugby.summary: Gregor Townsend reflected on the strides his Scotland side have made since their collapse against Argentina last autumn as they rounded off a long season with a comeback win over Fiji.
Rugby.body:
Gregor Townsend reflected on the strides his Scotland side have made since their collapse against Argentina last autumn as they rounded off a long season with a comeback win over Fiji.

Scotland somehow let a 21-0 half-time lead slip when they lost to the Pumas at Murrayfield in November. They soon lost in Italy in their Guinness Six Nations opener to leave Townsend facing criticism but they bounced back in impressive fashion and have now won five of their seven games since.

Rugby.title: The Springboks may have just found their skeleton key
Rugby.summary: After a succession of penalties, Wales are camped inside South Africa’s 22. It is the 50th minute of a game the Springboks have dominated, but the visitors are enjoying a rare period on the front foot.
Rugby.body:
After a succession of penalties, Wales are camped inside South Africa’s 22. It is the 50th minute of a game the Springboks have dominated, but the visitors are enjoying a rare period on the front foot. At 26-0 down, they are chasing their first points against the world champions in more than two hours of rugby. They might not get another chance before the final whistle.

Alex Mann carries and is nailed. Jac Morgan is drilled in contact. James Botham has a dart and is upended. Then, obscured in Tomos Williams’ blind spot, Paul de Villiers, in only his third Test, stoops low over the ball five metres from his own line. The whistle sounds. South African penalty. Pressure released.

Rugby.summary: Argentina heach coach Felipe Contepomi walks out of his news conference after the 31-24 defeat by England in the Nations Championship.
Rugby.body:
Argentina heach coach Felipe Contepomi walked out of his news conference after the 31-24 defeat by England in the Nations Championship. He said England's celebrations in the changing room next door showed a "lack of respect".

Contepomi had asked an England representative to stop the noise of the music and celebrations. Argentina were denied a try by the television match official in the final play of a chaotic match in Santiago del Estero.

Rugby.summary: Steve Tandy admitted Wales can not yet avoid pain on the Test stage after being nilled by South Africa for the second time in eight months.
Rugby.body:
Steve Tandy admitted Wales can not yet avoid pain on the Test stage after being nilled by South Africa for the second time in eight months. Wales were thrashed 43-0 by the Springboks on Saturday and rarely looked like scoring any points in Durban.

The Nations Championship defeat came after South Africa hammered them 73-0 in November, albeit Wales were without their England and France-based players on that occasion as the Cardiff clash was played outside the official Test window.

Rugby.title: Former All Blacks coach, Maori ABs captain headline Hurricanes departures
Rugby.summary: “Bailyn and Tevita, in particular, are half centurions and have made a huge contribution to the team over a number of years. We wish them both well on their journeys and their continued careers."
Rugby.body:
Former All Blacks assistant coach Bryn Evans has departed the Super Rugby Pacific champion Hurricanes, alongside four players ahead of next year’s competition. Hurricanes head coach Clark Laidlaw will be without the services of Bailyn Sullivan, Tom Allen, Tevita Mafileo, and Lucas Cashmore in the 2027 Super Rugby Pacific campaign.

Sullivan, an All Black XV member and the current Maori All Blacks captain, played over 50 games for the Wellington-based Super Rugby Pacific franchise. “I’ve thoroughly loved my time being part of such a special group of people during my time at the Hurricanes, so thank you to everyone that has been part of this journey. Stay hearty,” Sullivan said in the Hurricanes’ release.

Rugby.title: Super Rugby Aupiki final confirmed after Blues fend off Poua challenge
Rugby.summary: Prior to the top-of-the-table clash between the Blues and Matatu, the Hurricanes Poua took care of business against the Chiefs Manawa, 47-33, at Maidstone Park in Upper Hutt.
Rugby.body:
The Blues have held off a late playoff charge by the Hurricanes Poua to book their place in the 2026 Super Rugby Aupiki grand final against Matatu next weekend. The final, which will be hosted at the new One New Zealand Stadium in Christchurch, will be played between the Blues and Matatu for the second year running, after the Auckland-based franchise were crowned the 2025 champions.

Prior to the top-of-the-table clash between the Blues and Matatu, the Hurricanes Poua took care of business against the Chiefs Manawa, 47-33, at Maidstone Park in Upper Hutt. Astonishingly, it’s their fourth-straight Super Rugby Aupiki victory, which still wasn’t enough to make the grand final, even after posting their highest points total in a single match.

Rugby.title: Departing Wallabies coach Schmidt's message for Australian Rugby
Rugby.summary: Joe Schmidt has given Australian rugby one important piece of advice before setting off into the sunset.
Rugby.body:
Joe Schmidt has given Australian rugby one important piece of advice before setting off into the sunset – make sure Australia’s Super Rugby teams get better. Schmidt’s coaching stint at the Wallabies ended with a bang on Saturday night when Australia ran in nine tries to two in a crushing 57-10 Nations Championship win over Italy in Perth.

It marked Australia’s highest score in Schmidt’s two-and-a-half-year tenure and their largest on home soil since 2014. Schmidt ends his Wallabies reign with 12 wins and 19 losses – a disappointing result on paper.

Rugby.title: USA hold off Spain to remain undefeated in the Nations Cup
Rugby.summary: USA have held off a resilient Spain side by 29-22 in North Carolina to remain undefeated in the Nations Cup with three wins from three matches.
Rugby.body:
USA have held off a resilient Spain side by 29-22 in North Carolina to remain undefeated in the Nations Cup with three wins from three matches. The American forward pack, led by openside Paddy Ryan who finished with three turnovers, were able to come up with a handful of key turnovers in the final quarter to hold on for victory.

The Eagles led after three first half tries before Spain hit the front after turning the tide after half-time. A runaway intercept try to centre Martiniano Cian early in the second half by Spain drew level with the USA at 19-all.

The American forward pack, led by openside Paddy Ryan who finished with three turnovers, were able to come up with a handful of key turnovers in the final quarter to hold on for victory.

The Eagles led after three first half tries before Spain hit the front after turning the tide after half-time. A runaway intercept try to centre Martiniano Cian early in the second half by Spain drew level with the USA at 19-all.

Rugby.body:
Former scrum-half Matt Dawson described England's discipline as "verging on comical" after four players were shown yellow cards in the second half of their 31-24 win over Argentina.

England were twice reduced to 13 players in Santiago del Estero, including in the final three minutes as Argentina - who themselves had three players yellow-carded - attempted to overturn a 14-point deficit to salvage a draw.

Rugby.title: Nations Championship results, standings, fixtures & format
Rugby.summary: What is the Nations Championship? Who is winning? And when is next round of fixtures?
Rugby.body:
The Nations Championship pits the northern hemisphere teams who compete in the Six Nations - England, Ireland, Scotland, Wales, France and Italy - against southern hemisphere giants South Africa, New Zealand, Australia and Argentina, plus invited sides Fiji and Japan.

The geographically observant will note that Japan is actually about 2,500 miles north of the equator, so doesn't sit in the southern hemisphere. But the sport is rolling with it.

Rugby.body:
All Blacks first five-eighth Ruben Love was pulled from the field in the 56th minute against Ireland with fullback Damian McKenzie taking over to finish the game. Love received heavy strapping to his left knee after coming down awkwardly from an aerial contest with Irish winger Jimmy O’Brien, with the No.10 appearing to be tackled in the air.

The officials deemed it warranted a penalty but the All Blacks took the advantage by playing on and winning a 50-22 lineout, eventually scoring through McKenzie from close range after Love nearly scored himself.

Rugby.title: Ill-disciplined England beat Argentina in thriller after controversial late TMO call
Rugby.summary: England hold on to beat Argentina in a chaotic match in the Nations Championship after the hosts have a last-gasp try controversially ruled out in Santiago del Estero.
Rugby.body:
England held on to beat Argentina in a chaotic match in the Nations Championship after the hosts had a last-gasp try controversially ruled out in Santiago del Estero. With 13-man England leading 31-24, Argentina wing Bautista Delguy scored in the corner with the final play - leaving a difficult conversion to secure a draw.

Referee Angus Gardner had awarded the try on field, but television match official Brett Cronan insisted Delguy was in touch. While Gardner repeatedly suggested there was no clear evidence to overturn his original on-field call, the try was eventually chalked off.

Rugby.title: Tandy bitterly disappointed by South Africa drubbing
Rugby.summary: Steve Tandy commended his side's efforts but could not hide his disappointment with Wales' Nations Championship loss to South Africa.
Rugby.body:
Wales head coach Steve Tandy says he was bitterly disappointed to finish the season with a 43-0 hammering by South Africa. Tandy's side failed to score a single point once more against the Springboks, who ran out convincing Nations Championship winners in Durban.

The world champions won their previous meeting 73-0 in November when Wales conceded 11 tries and suffered their heaviest home defeat. South Africa were nowhere near as ruthless on home soil, but still scored seven tries with Jasper Wiese, Cobus Reinach, Jesse Kriel, Jaco Williams, Herschel Jantjies, Kurt-Lee Arendse and Paul de Villiers crossing.

Rugby.title: Wales held pointless again by seven-try South Africa
Rugby.summary: South Africa ease to a seven-try bonus-point victory over Wales in the third round of the Nations Championship in Durban.
Rugby.body:
South Africa eased to a seven-try bonus-point victory against Wales in the third round of the Nations Championship in Durban. Number eight Jasper Wiese, scrum-half Cobus Reinach, centre Jessie Kriel, wings Jaco Williams and Kurt-Lee Arendse, scrum-half Herschel Jantjies and flanker Paul de Villiers scored the tries for the double world champions.

The Springboks managed this comfortable success without star names like captain Siya Kolisi, Cheslin Kolbe, Ox Nche and Eben Etzebeth, who was one of seven locks missing. It was not as humiliating for Wales as the 73-0 record home loss to South Africa in Cardiff last November but the victory highlighted the gulf between the two nations.

Rugby.body:
Asher Opoku-Fordjour has been withdrawn from England’s bench for their clash with Argentina in Santiago del Estero because of concussion. Opoku-Fordjour failed a HIA after taking a head knock in training so George Kloska returns to the replacements as tighthead prop cover after making his debut against Fiji last Saturday.

Kloska has had a reduced training load this week due to a tight back but is fit enough to participate in the final fixture of England’s July tour. Opoku-Fordjour, the Sale front row who covers both sides of the scrum, was set to make his first appearance in Argentina since being the target of racial abuse by a small group of Pumas fans in San Juan last year.

Rugby.body:
Josh Canham has become the first Wallabies lock to score a Test hat-trick as Australia farewelled coach Joe Schmidt in style with a 57-10 demolition of Italy in Perth. The world No.8 Wallabies entered Saturday night’s Nations Championship clash having lost nine of their past 10 Test matches, including six on the trot.

But from the very outset Australia’s determination was clear to see, with the home side running in six tries to one in a dominant first half to open up a match-winning 38-5 lead by the break in front of 19,268 fans.

Rugby.title: All Blacks leave Irish with familiar sinking feeling
Rugby.summary: After a six-try defeat by New Zealand in Eden Park, Ireland have now lost six games in a row against the All Blacks, France and South Africa.
Rugby.body:
As the All Blacks extended their long unbeaten run at Eden Park to 53 matches with a 40-21 victory over Ireland, it was the continuation of a newer trend that will be of concern to Andy Farrell.

The 19-point defeat means Farrell's side have lost their past six contests against New Zealand, France and South Africa by double-digit margins. Since the retirement of Johnny Sexton after the 2023 World Cup, Ireland have won just two such games, against a 14-man France to start the 2024 Six Nations and against the Springboks in Durban thanks to Ciaran Frawley's last-gasp drop goal later that same year.

Rugby.summary: The All Blacks started strongly, leading 14-0 in the opening half hour before Ireland hit back through Jack Conan with Luke Jacobson in the bin.

Rugby.title: All Blacks punish Ireland in dominant Eden Park win
Rugby.summary: Ruthless New Zealand score five tries to overwhelm Ireland and preserve their 32-year unbeaten run at Eden Park in a largely one-sided Nations Championship contest.
Rugby.body:
Ruthless New Zealand scored six tries to overwhelm Ireland and preserve their 32-year unbeaten run at Eden Park in a largely one-sided Nations Championship contest. Buoyed by victories over France and Italy, the All Blacks punished a litany of first-half Irish errors as Patrick Tuipulotu, Ardie Savea, Will Jordan and Asafo Aumua all crossed to secure the bonus point.

Ireland's solitary first-half score from Jack Conan came after Luke Jacobson was yellow carded for a dangerous clearout on Josh van der Flier, with the New Zealand flanker avoiding a red card following an off-field review.

Rugby.title: Ireland player ratings vs New Zealand | Nations Championship 2026
Rugby.summary: Ireland player ratings: A mammoth task awaited Andy Farrell's men at Eden Park, but this was one in which Ireland repeatedly shot themselves in the proverbial foot.
Rugby.body:
Ireland player ratings: A mammoth task awaited Andy Farrell’s men at Eden Park, but this was one in which Ireland repeatedly shot themselves in the proverbial foot. Endless errors, ill-discipline and basic execution failures meant they never really got a look-in, while the All Blacks were utterly ruthless whenever an opportunity presented itself. Ireland’s defensive system malfunctioned too often and too many tackles were slipped.

To their credit, they fought back valiantly and stopped the scoreboard from becoming truly ugly, but much of this 40-21 defeat felt like damage limitation. Not flawless, but deserves some credit for a scrum that held up better than many expected against quality opposition. There were a few costly pre-engagement penalties and he was partly implicated in the breakdown that led to New Zealand’s opening try, but there was enough set-piece stability to prevent things getting completely out of hand.

Rugby.summary: Scotland flanker Hamish Watson has signed for Castres after leaving Edinburgh.
Rugby.body:
Scotland flanker Hamish Watson has signed for Castres after leaving Edinburgh. The French Top 14 club moved to recruit the 34-year-old after Dalton Papali'i was ruled out long-term after undergoing surgery for a ruptured Achilles tendon.

Watson, who ended last season on loan to Leicester Tigers, revealed he had to make his mind up quickly after being contacted by Castres. "The opportunity to perform in French rugby is a fantastic opportunity for me," he told the club website after agreeing a one-year contract.

Rugby.title: Wales aim to defy the odds in South Africa
Rugby.summary: After a 10-month campaign that started for most players last August, one more challenge awaits Wales in the South African coastal city of Durban.
Rugby.body:
After a 10-month campaign that started for most players last August, one more challenge awaits Wales after they arrived this week in the South African coastal city of Durban. Steve Tandy's side face the ultimate test, with the daunting challenge of meeting the double world champions on their own turf.

Hardly anybody will give Wales a chance. They are now ranked 12th in the world following the 35-21 defeat to Argentina and they lost 73-0 to the Springboks in Cardiff last autumn.

Castres marquee signing Papali’i suffered the injury during training at the very start of his career in France and had surgery on Wednesday. He made six appearances for his former academy club between March and June after joining from Edinburgh, where he’d fallen out of favour under head coach Sean Everitt.

Rugby.title: Five pointers as England aim to maintain psychological ‘stranglehold’ over Pumas
Rugby.summary: Benching Caluori, classy Slade, Martin's return, 'different animal' Heyes and a lurking threat to Van Poortvliet as England prepare for Pumas.
Rugby.body:
If England can manage to inflict a measure of revenge on Argentina for their football counterparts’ defeat in the Fifa World Cup semi-final this weekend, it will be their sixth successive win over the Pumas.

England’s recent record against Argentina is better than that of any other nation – including world champions South Africa. The stranglehold they have exerted in the fixture of late extends back to a 30-29 defeat at Twickenham in November 2022.

Rugby.title: 'These fellas are Gods'
Rugby.summary: The All Blacks are undefeated at their Auckland stronghold in 52 Tests, and the place holds plenty harrowing memories for the touring Irish.
Rugby.body:
Donncha O’Callaghan and Moss Keane hated touring New Zealand. One part, O’Callaghan reasoned, was leaving an Irish summer to land in a Kiwi winter. “The biggest part,” he added, “was every tour of New Zealand involved playing the All Blacks. Those matches never turned out the way we hoped.”

O’Callaghan toured New Zealand in 2005 with the British & Irish Lions and 2006 with Ireland. He returned there in 2011 for the World Cup. When players of his generation think of Eden Park, their minds hark back to the one good memory they have – defeating Australia 15-6 – there in that 2011 tournament.

Rugby.title: There's been an update on the Gonzalo Quesada match-day ban
Rugby.summary: Italy head coach Gonzalo Quesada has received an update one-match suspension and a formal warning following an independent disciplinary hearing into comments...
Rugby.body:
Italy head coach Gonzalo Quesada has received an update one-match suspension and a formal warning following an independent disciplinary hearing into comments he made about match officials after Italy’s Nations Championship defeat to New Zealand.

Quesada said referee Luc Ramos was “super poor” and implied the margin of the defeat was increased due to the officiating of the French referee. Quesada was initially handed an automatic two-match ban under World Rugby’s Match Official Abuse Sanction Process, which was introduced to deal with public criticism of referees and other match officials. However, the former Argentina international exercised his right to refer the case to an independent disciplinary committee for a full de novo hearing.

Rugby.title: England could walk off if players racially abused in Argentina
Rugby.summary: Captain Jamie George says England are considering the prospect of walking off the pitch should any of their players suffer racial abuse against Argentina.
Rugby.body:
Captain Jamie George says England are considering the prospect of walking off the pitch should any of their players suffer racial abuse against Argentina on Saturday. Last year's win in San Juan was marred by abuse targeting England replacements Asher Opoku-Fordjour and Chandler Cunningham-South.

Governing body World Rugby condemned the incident but were unable to identify any perpetrators. The last meeting between the teams, in November, ended in a heated exchange, with Argentina coach Felipe Contepomi calling England flanker Tom Curry a "bully" who swore at him and pushed him in the tunnel at Allianz Stadium.

Rugby.summary: The powerful Harlequins and England U20 second-row discusses his rugby journey and having Austin Healey question his age.
Rugby.body:
Keith and Sarah Williams were talented basketball players in their youth, before setting down roots in the leafy environs of Staines-upon-Thames, but with a growing brood, there was no obvious outlet to mould them into the next LeBron James or Victor Wembanyama, so with five children climbing the walls, they agreed the next best thing would be to ferry those willing to the nearest rugby club: London Irish Amateurs.

Elliot, the second eldest, had a natural disposition for rugby and 14 years later, will be staring down the Haka tomorrow as England U20s look to secure a third-placed finish at the Junior World Championship.

Rugby.body:
Wales lock Alaw Pyrs has signed a new contract to keep her at Premiership Women's Rugby side Gloucester-Hartpury. The 20-year-old represented her country at the 2025 Women's Rugby World Cup as well as the 2025 and 2026 Women's Six Nations.

Rugby.body:
Jerry Collins’ 18-year-old daughter Honey Kerslake has signed her first senior contract with JAECOO Premiership Women’s Rugby club Exeter Chiefs. In 2015, while playing for French club Narbonne, Collins was tragically killed in a car crash. He won 48 caps for the All Blacks and played at two Rugby World Cups.

Rugby.title: Inside rugby's greatest production factory
Rugby.summary: On Saturday Wales face South Africa - a nation who never seem to run out of international-class players. Are there lessons the tourists can learn?
Rugby.body:
The Springboks' seemingly endless supply of talent is the envy of world rugby. So why does South Africa continue to produce world-class players at a rate few nations can match?

Every rugby nation wants what South Africa have: four World Cups. World Cup winners have retired. Others have headed overseas. Yet the Springboks never seem to run out of international-class players.

Rugby.title: Blacklock 'looking forward to next chapter' after Saracens exit
Rugby.summary: Former Scotland international Beth Blacklock has left JAECOO Premiership Women's Rugby champions Saracens for France.
Rugby.body:
Former Scotland international Beth Blacklock has left JAECOO Premiership Women’s Rugby champions Saracens for France. The 28-year-old centre, who won six caps for Scotland between 2023 and 2025, has signed with newly promoted AXA Élite 1 Feminine side Stade Rochelais.

Upon the announcement of her departure, Blacklock revealed that her father, Danny, also lived and played rugby in the city. Blacklock said: “I loved my time at Saracens and the opportunities the club gave me, but I’ve always wanted to use rugby as a chance to travel and experience playing in France. I’m excited to play in the city where my dad lived and played, and I’m looking forward to this next chapter.”

Rugby.title: England make late change to Argentina plans to block out the outside noise
Rugby.summary: Hundreds of thousands of Argentina fans gathered in the capital on Wednesday night to celebrate the semi-final win over Thomas Tuchel’s side.
Rugby.body:
England have been forced to change hotel in Buenos Aires on Sunday night to avoid being caught up in any celebrations should Argentina win the World Cup. Hundreds of thousands of fans gathered around the famous Obelisk on the Plaza de la Republica on Wednesday night to celebrate the 2-1 semi-final victory over Thomas Tuchel’s side – right outside where England have been based in the Argentinian capital.

Fireworks were let off throughout the night and earplugs were issued to players and staff to help with sleep amid the noise, while steel fencing was erected around the hotel as a precautionary measure.

Rugby.body:
Gloucester’s search for a new scrum coach appears to have come to an end with former Prem prop Ryan Bower understood to have been appointed as Trevor Woodman’s replacement. RWC 2003 winner Woodman has chosen to leave Kingsholm after 12 years as a player and coach to join Stuart Lancaster’s backroom team at URC outfit Connacht, and they have now turned to Bower.

Working to a limited rugby budget, Gloucester’s rugby management were unable to cast the net far and wide in their search for a new scrum coach and have opted to go with someone right on their doorstep.

Rugby.title: The Fijians who lit up Scottish rugby 10,000 miles from home
Rugby.summary: As the teams prepare to meet at Murrayfield, Scotland fans will reflect fondly upon the Flying Fijians who made riveting contributions to their rugby community.
Rugby.body:
For Scotland fans flocking to Murrayfield this weekend, a clash with the Flying Fijians will evoke painful memories. Scotland are one of a handful of elite opposition to play Test matches on the Fijian islands, and were well beaten on their past two visits – most recently, a 29-14 defeat only 12 months ago.

Facing Fiji will also stoke warmer recollections. For in some senses, the nations share a rich history – from the iconic ‘Weegies from Fiji’ who helped Glasgow swagger to a maiden title, to the lesser heralded names and even the coaches who have played a hand in the development of both sides.

Rugby.title: What Welsh rugby has to improve to avoid regressing to the dark days
Rugby.summary: Steve Tandy will finish off a challenging campaign at the home of the World Champions South Africa knowing there is work to do
Rugby.body:
Before Wales encountered South Africa on their ill-fated tour of 1998, they faced Zimbabwe in Harare. As preparation for a match against the Springboks, the date at the Police Grounds was the equivalent of riding a 1970s Raleigh Chopper around the block in readiness for a crack at the Tour de France.

Let’s just say that at breakfast in the tourists’ hotel the morning after the game with Nick Mallett’s Boks, there wasn’t a yellow jersey in sight. An outing in San Juan against Argentina this time means the step up will be lessened, though an emphatic defeat and a 5,700-mile trek across continents and five time zones hardly ticks every box when it comes to perfect preparation. There again, no one said the new Nations Championship would be without challenges.

They host England this week, looking to follow the lead of their footballing colleagues. Pumas head coach Felipe Contepomi played in the 2007 World Cup when Argentina reached the final four for the first time – a run that included wins over France, Ireland and Scotland.

Rugby.summary: Charlie Abel will make a hard-earned debut for the USA Men’s Eagles in a World Rugby Nations Cup clash with Spain.
Rugby.body:
At 34 years of age, Australian-born prop Charlie Abel will make a hard-earned debut for the USA Men’s Eagles in a World Rugby Nations Cup clash with Spain. Abel initially moved Stateside ahead of the 2021 Major League Rugby season, having played for two clubs since.

Following stints with the NSW Waratahs and Melbourne Rebels, Abel won an MLR Championship with the LA Giltinis as a rookie. The front-rower has since become a two-time champ, starting in the big dance as the Chicago Hounds defeated California Legion on June 22.

There are five changes to the starting team, with prop Alex Hewitt promoted to start at tighthead and Finn McLeod joining in the second row; the rest of the forward pack remains unchanged. In the backline, Jackson Hughan has come in at halfback, with Lautasi Etuale added on the wing and Logan Williams at fullback.

New Zealand emerges from a dramatic semi-final loss to France with an injury to first-five Mika Muliaina, pushing Cohen Norie into No.10 from fullback, and an illness to left winger David Lewai.

Rugby.title: Tupou Vaa'i reveals past All Black who inspired him to become a 'menace'
Rugby.summary: Tupou Vaa'i is leaning into his reputation as a "menace" on the rugby field, and has revealed who inspired his emergence as an antagoniser.
Rugby.body:
Tupou Vaa’i is leaning into his reputation as a “menace” on the rugby field, and has revealed who inspired his emergence as an antagoniser. The 26-year-old is in his seventh season with the All Blacks, having come into the squad as a lock during the iconic second-row partnership of Brodie Retallick and Sam Whitelock, with Scott Barrett also in the mix and later pushing into the starting team.

While minutes were hard to come by for the youngster, the mentorship he was exposed to gave him every chance to grow his game on the training park, and when his time came in 2024, Vaa’i quickly established himself as one of New Zealand’s premier forwards.

Rugby.title: Wallabies’ second-half fades reveal a pathway to victory in Perth
Rugby.summary: You will have heard plenty of rugby coaches talk of the “controllables” and how you must control the things you can and not worry about the things you cannot.
Rugby.body:
You will have heard plenty of rugby coaches talk of the “controllables” and how you must control the things you can and not worry about the things you cannot. This seemingly obvious adage is very helpful in understanding the Wallabies in the past few weeks, particularly for understanding the second-half capitulations.

While identifying that “second-half fades” are the problem is a good initial step, much more forensic work must be done to understand these woes and know how to fix them. In Sydney, the Wallabies lost that second half to Ireland because they had very little ball or territory due to their reserves coming on and conceding far too many penalties and a yellow card.

Rugby.title: I've not found my feet back in rugby - Rees-Zammit
Rugby.summary: Wales wing Louis Rees-Zammit ready to make a bigger impact next season after a first year back in rugby.
Rugby.body:
Louis Rees-Zammit says he has not settled back into rugby as quickly as he would have liked during his first year back in the sport. The 25-year-old announced almost 12 months ago that he was returning to his original sport from American football after trying to break into the NFL.

Rees-Zammit has featured in 10 out of the 11 Wales internationals played in the 2025-26 campaign, with eight starts and two replacement appearances. The Bristol back only missed the 73-0 defeat against South Africa in November 2025 because he was ineligible as he played for an English club and the match fell outside World Rugby's international window.

Rugby.title: Tommy Freeman: ‘I always had to work really hard to get what I wanted. I always felt like I was up against it’
Rugby.summary: The versatile wing or centre may be a first-choice for England now but his route to the top has not always been smooth.
Rugby.body:
There are easier weeks to be in Argentina as an England international. England’s team hotel sits on Avenida 9 de Julio, one of the busiest roads in Buenos Aires, where the celebrations following Argentina’s dramatic World Cup semi-final victory over England on Wednesday carried on long into the night.

For Tommy Freeman, the backdrop has provided a timely reminder of what it means to represent your country. “I kind of have to pinch myself on game day. You’re doing what you love, you’ve grown up doing it and you’re doing it to represent not only yourself, but everyone who supports the country and is part of it. Especially now, it’s probably heightened, with the football at the front of mind.”

Rugby.title: Smith to wear special jersey as Scotland remember Hastings
Rugby.summary: Scott Hastings, who died in May aged 61, will be remembered at Murrayfield on Saturday as Scotland host Fiji in their final game of the summer series.
Rugby.body:
Scott Hastings will be remembered at Murrayfield on Saturday as Scotland host Fiji in their final game of the Nations Championship. The centre, a much-loved and much-decorated player, passed away suddenly in May aged 61. The tributes that came after his passing said much about his reputation across the rugby world.

Warm and gregarious, Hastings made 65 Test appearances for his country, a record at the time. He wore the number 13 jersey with distinction. Against Fiji, Ollie Smith will wear a special version of that 13 shirt. The number 13 will be done in gold and inside the numbers will be the names of the teams Hastings turned out for in his career as well as some of his notable achievements.

Rugby.body:

Vui, 33, tested positive in August 2023 for 19-norandrosterone, an indicator for the steroid nandrolone, before that year's Rugby World Cup, in which he represented Samoa. He was immediately suspended by World Rugby but has always denied knowingly using the banned substance.

Rugby.title: Jake White: Test rugby has changed a lot since I was Bok coach
Rugby.summary: I’ve been on a hunting trip into the bush this week. It’s given me plenty of pause for thought about rugby’s direction of travel in recent weeks and where it’s heading…
Rugby.body:
I’ve been on a hunting trip into the bush this week. It’s given me plenty of pause for thought about rugby’s direction of travel in recent weeks and where it’s heading… When I was coaching internationally, and even before my time, the Tri-Nations teams used to have end of season tours to the Northern Hemisphere and correspondingly we’d return the favour by hosting the Northern Hemisphere sides in their summer.

What would often happen is that when we’d play England and Twickenham, or France at the Parc des Princes and latterly Stade de France, we’d get drilled. Fans would say, ‘ya, but the South are at a big disadvantage because the Northern Hemisphere sides are up to speed and fresh and we’re running on fumes’, whereas on the flip-side we were at an advantage in the their summer because they were at the end of their season, carrying injuries, fatigued or understrength and we’d just come out of Super Rugby and were fit and firing, but looking at the last two weekends, I’d ask, ‘what’s changed?’ You’re getting some humdingers. 33-31 between Ireland and Australia, 34-32 between New Zealand and France and while 42-28 seems like a comfortable win for South Africa against Scotland, it was anything but.

Rugby.title: Vusi Moyo: Why has a 20-year-old with barely any senior rugby been trusted to start at No.10 for South Africa?
Rugby.summary: The Springboks' new fly-half has played one game of senior rugby but his coaches are confident he will swiftly 'make you believe'.
Rugby.body:
When Vusi Moyo first entered the Sharks environment, Joey Mongalo, a senior coach at the club, gave the 18-year-old fly-half some homework. The assignment was straightforward. The teenager, fresh out of school, had to conduct a SWOT analysis of his own rugby. He was asked to identify his strengths, his weaknesses, the opportunities available to him and the threats that might prevent him from fulfilling his potential.

Mongalo expected a single page of hastily assembled notes. What he received was a four-page typed document. Most of it was devoted to the things Moyo could not yet do. “I thought, ‘Wow, there’s something special here,’” says Mongalo, who worked with Moyo during his brief time with the Sharks’ United Rugby Championship squad. “This is not just a future fly-half. This is a future quarterback who’s got the capacity to think about his game in depth, know himself well and have good self-awareness for an 18-year-old.”

Rugby.title: 'I must now face the facts': France's Romane Ménager ends playing career
Rugby.summary: France’s two-time Grand Slam-winning back-row Romane Ménager said it was ‘time to listen to her body’ as she called time on her playing career.
Rugby.body:
France’s two-time Grand Slam-winning back-row Romane Ménager said it was ‘time to listen to her body’ as she called time on her playing career at the age of 29. “After two seasons of doing everything possible to return to the field in the best possible conditions, and thanks to the support of competent, caring and dedicated people, I must now face the facts,” the 68-cap international wrote in a social media post.

“It is time to listen to my body. Following difficulties in recovering after several concussions, and after numerous discussions with the medical staff, we have made the decision to end my playing career in order to preserve my health.”

Rugby.body:
Ireland head coach Andy Farrell says Jimmy O'Brien is "on top of his game" heading into the Nations Championship match against New Zealand in Auckland. Rugby.title: Scarlets rugby jersey from legendary 1972 win over All Blacks to be auctioned
Rugby.summary: That day in 1972 is known locally as "the day the pubs ran dry", following major celebrations.
Rugby.body:
A Llanelli rugby jersey from the club's historic 1972 win over the All Blacks is to be sold at auction for the first time. Tommy David was part of the famous side that beat New Zealand 9-3 in front of a capacity crowd at Stradey Park.

The day has become known locally as "the day the pubs ran dry", following major celebrations after the match all over the town. David's red Umbro No 6 jersey is expected to fetch up to £15,000 when it is sold on July 27 by Rogers Jones Auctioneers in Cardiff.

Toulouse scrum-half Paul Graou is set to make his France debut from the bench on Saturday against Japan in round three of the Nations Championship. The 28-year-old, who serves as back-up to Antoine Dupont for the Top 14 champions, is the only debutant in the squad for the match against Eddie Jones’ Brave Blossoms in Tokyo.

Les Bleus’ boss Fabien Galthie has made four changes to his starting XV from the side that triumphed over Australia 42-26 last week, with a completely new front-row. Jefferson Poirot, Maxime Lamothe and Regis Montagne will start this week, with last week’s hooker, Peato Mauvaka, starting on the bench.

Rugby.title: Fiji Prime Minister responds to Flying Fijians' poor start to Nations Championship
Rugby.summary: Fiji Prime Minister Sitiveni Rabuka has defended the appointment of interim Flying Fijians head coach Senirusi Seruvakula and insists two games is too soon to deliver a verdict on his leadership of the squad that has suffered losses to Wales and England.
Rugby.body:
Fiji Prime Minister Sitiveni Rabuka has defended the appointment of interim Flying Fijians head coach Senirusi Seruvakula and insists two games is too soon to deliver a verdict on his leadership of the squad that has suffered losses to Wales and England.

Seruvakula replaced former head coach Mick Byrne and Rabuka told Fiji media he had always supported the idea of a local coach to lead the Flying Fijians. “We should give the process time,” said Rabuka, the former Flying Fijians player. “Let’s see whether the argument that a local coach better understands the players, and the players better understand the coach, proves correct.

Rugby.title: World Rugby statement: Gonzalo Quesada banned under new match official abuse process
Rugby.summary: Italy head coach Gonzalo Quesada has become the first coach sanctioned under World Rugby's new Match Official Abuse Sanction Process after being handed an automatic two-match suspension for comments made following his side's Nations Championship defeat to New Zealand.
Rugby.body:
Italy head coach Gonzalo Quesada has become the first coach sanctioned under World Rugby’s new Match Official Abuse Sanction Process after being handed an automatic two-match suspension for comments made following his side’s Nations Championship defeat to New Zealand.

The Azzurri fell 47-17 to the All Blacks in round two of the Nations Championship in Wellington on Saturday, with the Argentine criticising referee Luc Ramos after the match. World Rugby confirmed the punishment on Wednesday, with Quesada banned from all match-day activities, including being present in the stadium, ahead of their round three fixture with Australia on Saturday in Perth. The governing body also confirmed the Italian boss has the right to appeal the sanction before a full judicial committee.

Rugby.title: The All Blacks don't need the Eden Park record
Rugby.summary: The All Blacks are two games into a new coaching era. They’re embedding a new first five-eighth and trying different combinations across the park.
Rugby.body:
I guess people have to talk about something. In recent days, it’s that the All Blacks failed to beat Italy 100-0 in Wellington. In the time between now and Saturday, it’ll be about Ireland’s past deeds and how New Zealand’s enviable record at Eden Park could be in peril.

The All Blacks are two games into a new coaching era. They’re embedding a new first five-eighth and trying different combinations across the park. They have some big matches coming up against South Africa and then a Rugby World Cup next year. The rest of their Test schedule is hardly worth a mention.

Rugby.summary: All Blacks head coach Dave Rennie says he wanted to field a bigger pack against Ireland, and has done so by moving Tupou Vaa'i from the second row to the loose forwards.
Rugby.body:
All Blacks head coach Dave Rennie says he wanted to field a bigger pack against Ireland, and has done so by moving Tupou Vaa’i from the second row to the loose forwards. Vaa’i will link up with Luke Jacobson and Ardie Savea in the back row, 11 months after last running out in the N0.6 jersey for New Zealand against Los Pumas in Argentina.

It will be the 26-year-old’s sixth start on the blindside flank at Test level, with his first appearance there coming against France in the 2023 Rugby World Cup opener. Experimenting with the No.6 jersey remains a touchy subject for All Blacks fans, with the scars from Scott Barrett’s brief trial in the position in the 2019 Rugby World Cup semi-final loss to England proving slow to heal.

Rugby.title: Simione Kuruvoli learns fate after red card against England
Rugby.summary: Assessing the play this week, a disciplinary committee found Kuruvoli guilty of what it described as "physical abuse in contravention of Law 9.12."
Rugby.body:
A disciplinary committee has handed Simione Kuruvoli a four-week suspension for his act of “physical abuse” that resulted in a permanent red card against England. The Fijian halfback was spotted kicking England prop Ellis Genge in the chest as he left a breakdown in the 42nd minute of his team’s 73-8 defeat at Hill Dickinson Stadium last weekend.

Replay footage showed Genge had initially held Kuruvoli back, but had released the halfback by the time Kuruvoli lashed back and struck the prop’s body. After reviewing the replay, referee Holly Davidson issued a permanent red card, and Fiji, already trailing 35-3, went down to 14 men for the entire second half. To make matters worse for his team, the try Fiji had scored moments after Kuruvoli’s dangerous act was scrubbed out.

Rugby.title: Referee Barrett-Theron stands down after cancer diagnosis
Rugby.summary: One of the world's leading female referees, Aimee Barrett-Theron, has stood down from officiating after being diagnosed with breast cancer.
Rugby.body:
Aimee Barrett-Theron, one of the world's leading female referees, has stood down from officiating after being diagnosed with breast cancer. The 39 year-old South African is the most-capped female international referee after taking charge of 52 Tests.

"I've recently been diagnosed with breast cancer," she said in a statement. "The good news is that it's treatable, and I'm working with an incredible team of specialists who are fully aligned with the goal of getting me healthy and back on the field in a few months' time."

Rugby.title: New KSSSA rugby sevens champions beckon as defending kings fall
Rugby.summary: New KSSSA rugby sevens champions beckon as defending kings fall Mozzart Sport Kenya
Rugby.body:
Reading Time: 4min | Wed. 15.07.26. | 18:39 The stage is set for another thrilling chapter in Kenya Secondary Schools Sports Association (KSSSA) Rugby Sevens as the country's best boys' and girls' teams prepare to battle for national honors at the 2026 Term Two Games in Thika.

Unlike last year, this edition arrives with both competitions wide open. The defending boys' champions, St. Peter's Mumias, will not be part of the national championship after their title defense ended in the Western Region semifinals, while the girls' competition promises another fascinating battle as Kinale Girls seek to retain the title they won in 2025.

Rugby.title: Halse 'buzzing' to ignite Waratahs season after six injury-plagued months
Rugby.summary: Caitlyn Halse bombastically celebrating to the crowd after scoring against the United States has gone down as one of the iconic images of Women's Rugby World Cup 2025.
Rugby.body:
Caitlyn Halse bombastically celebrating to the crowd after scoring against the United States has gone down as one of the iconic images of Women’s Rugby World Cup 2025. It also signalled her arrival on the international stage.

Now, after a long sideline stint, the young full-back – affectionately known as “The Kid” by her Wallaroos teammates – is set to finally make her return off the bench this weekend against the Western Force in Perth, and her return comes at a critical time for the NSW Waratahs.

Doncaster Knights director of rugby Dean Richards is pulling together an experienced coaching team to launch an assault on the Champ next season, with Carl Hogg and Alan Dickens joining his coaching staff.

Rugby.title: Cobus Reinach's 'not an individual sport' message to Bok debutant
Rugby.summary: Reinach, who came on in the 51st minute of that Cardiff cake walk, has been practising with Moyo and is confident the partnership will be seamless even in the daunting Test arena.
Rugby.body:
Experienced scrum half Cobus Reinach is backing Springbok new boy Vusi Moyo to thrive in the No.10 jersey but is steering clear of predicting another hammering of Wales. The last time the Springboks played Wales they delivered a 73-0 thrashing in Cardiff, which may explain why head coach Rassie Erasmus believes the time is right to give Moyo a debut, particularly on his home ground.

Reinach, who came on in the 51st minute of that Cardiff cake walk, has been practising with Moyo and is confident the partnership will be seamless even in the daunting Test arena.

Rugby.title: 'I really want to enjoy my rugby': Phillips trades London for the South West
Rugby.summary: Carys Phillips has swapped Harlequins for Exeter Chiefs ahead of the 2026/27 JAECOO Premiership Women's Rugby season.
Rugby.body:
Carys Phillips has swapped Harlequins for Exeter Chiefs ahead of the 2026/27 JAECOO Premiership Women’s Rugby season. The 87-cap, 12-year Wales international joined Harlequins in 2023 from Worcester Warriors.

The 33-year-old’s arrival is timely following Emily Tuttosi’s departure from Devon for a coaching role in her native Canada. As Harlequins missed out on a play-off space in 2025/26, Phillips made 15 appearances for the West London club and scored four tries.

Rugby.title: 'I think Pollock is our best player... he should be starting'
Rugby.summary: Former Wales fly-half Dan Biggar has praised England head coach Steve Borthwick for the way he has managed back-row Henry Pollock so far in his Test career, saying the 21-year-old is suited to playing from the bench.
Rugby.body:
Former Wales fly-half Dan Biggar has praised England head coach Steve Borthwick for the way he has managed back-row Henry Pollock so far in his Test career, saying the 21-year-old is suited to playing from the bench.

Pollock has started only one of his 12 Test appearances since making his debut against Wales in the 2025 Six Nations, which came this year against Ireland, a match Biggar has described as his “poorest outing”.

Rugby.title: Rob Baxter explains why he thinks Julian Heaven will come good at Exeter
Rugby.summary: Heaven signed from the NSW Waratahs, making three starts in 13 appearances last season.
Rugby.body:
Julian Heaven had a difficult first season with Exeter Chiefs, but Director of Rugby Rob Baxter admits that he has seen a lot of players in the same situation in his years at the club, only for them to bounce back in their second campaign.

Baxter says it happens a lot to players who move to Devon from abroad, like Heaven, 25, who was one of three Australians who moved to Sandy Park last season, all with varying degrees of success, the most successful being Tom Hooper.

Rugby.title: Wales hooker Phillips moves to Exeter
Rugby.summary: Exeter Chiefs sign Wales hooker Carys Phillips for the 2026-27 Premiership Women's Rugby season.
Rugby.body:
Exeter Chiefs have signed Wales hooker Carys Phillips for the 2026-27 Premiership Women's Rugby season. The 33-year-old, who joins from Harlequins, has played in four Women's World Cups and won 87 caps for Wales since making her debut in 2013.

She recently followed in the footsteps of her father Rowland when she played for the Barbarians, becoming the first daughter and father to play for the famous team. Phillips is the second Wales forward to move to Sandy Park this month after prop Maisie Davies agreed a move.

Rugby.title: Why Bromley-born Aaron Grandidier-Nkanang, France's two try debutant, owes a debt to English rugby
Rugby.summary: Olympic Gold medallist, Aaron Grandidier-Nkanang's two-try debut is a tale of being honed in England but going to French finishing school
Rugby.body:
Aaron Grandidier Nkanang marked his debut for France with a brace of tries in their 42-26 thrashing of Australia last week. It was a momentous day for the 26-year-old winger, and an emotional one. In a live pitchside interview shortly after the match, Grandidier Nkanang was asked what was going through his mind. “I’m thinking about the journey, about rugby sevens, because without rugby sevens I wouldn’t be here today.,” he replied. “I’m thinking of my partner, my parents and my mates in London.”

That must be a first, a Frenchman thanking his friends in London for getting him to where he is today. But Grandidier Nkanang is not your run of the mill Bleu. Grandidier Nkanang was born in Bromley, Kent, to a British-Nigerian father and French mother. All his youth rugby was played in England, including some matches for Kent U18, and then in his nineteenth year he signed terms with Brive. For the first years of his professional career, Grandidier Nkanang’s speciality was Sevens and he was a member of the French squad that won gold in the 2024 Paris Olympics.

Rugby.title: England bunker down in Buenos Aires wary of backlash
Rugby.summary: England's rugby squad is not wearing any team-branded kit in public as FIFA World Cup fever grips the Argentinian capital.
Rugby.body:
Tommy Freeman fears a Pumas backlash on Saturday if England win their football World Cup semi-final against Argentina. Steve Borthwick’s squad are based in Buenos Aires until Thursday when they head to Santiago del Estero in the north of the country for the final assignment of their 25,000-mile July tour.

As a precautionary step, they are not wearing any team-branded kit in public as interest in the clash between Thomas Tuchel’s side and the current World Cup holders grips the Argentinian capital.

Rugby.title: Daughter of ex-Springbok back included in Junior Springbok Women squad
Rugby.summary: The daughter of 38-cap Springbok Men international Andre Snyman has been included in a Junior Springbok Women squad ahead of a series against the USA Women U20.
Rugby.body:
The daughter of 38-cap Springbok Men international Andre Snyman has been included in a Junior Springbok Women squad ahead of a series against the USA Women U20. Keira Snyman, 18, has been included as an additional player in the 30-player squad and can play on the wing or at centre. She has also spent time in England Rugby and USA Rugby age grade camps. The teenager was born in Durban but raised in the USA and England.

After a number of standout performances for invitational sevens teams last summer, Snyman caught the eye of England selectors. Already she had been named in USA U18 sevens camps but has spent the majority of this season in England.

Rugby.title: Impressive win over Springboks helps USA climb World Rugby rankings
Rugby.summary: The USA Women's Eagles have climbed back to eighth in the World Rugby rankings thanks to their 26-19 win against the Springbok Women last weekend.
Rugby.body:
The USA Women’s Eagles have climbed back to eighth in the World Rugby rankings thanks to their 26-19 win against the Springbok Women last weekend. A 34-21 defeat against South Africa one week earlier in Johannesburg had seen Jack Hanratty’s team fall to ninth behind their Pacific Four Series rivals the Wallaroos.

An instant return to winning ways in Pretoria means that the World Rugby rankings read the same as they did a fortnight ago. Hanratty made seven changes to his starting XV for the Pretoria Test and quickly reaped the rewards as braces for Hope Rogers and Telesi Uhatafe provided the North Americans with a suitable buffer between themselves and their hosts.

Rugby.title: Stage set for Faf de Klerk return against the Lions
Rugby.summary: South Africa scrum-half Faf de Klerk is set to make his Cheetahs debut this Sunday in round one of the Currie Cup against the Lions.
Rugby.body:
South Africa scrum-half Faf de Klerk is set to make his Cheetahs debut this Sunday in round one of the Currie Cup against the Lions. The 34-year-old’s return to South Africa was confirmed in April following four years with the Yokohama Canon Eagles in Japan Rugby League One. Prior to that, the double World Cup winner spent four years with Sale Sharks in England, meaning his Cheetahs debut will be his first club game in South Africa in almost a decade.

The 60-cap Springbok was omitted from Rassie Erasmus’ South Africa squad for the Nations Championship last month, with the world number ones facing Wales on Saturday in round three following victories over England and Scotland.

Rugby.title: Two-time Olympian Brown among 10 Loughborough Lightning re-signings
Rugby.summary: GB Sevens captain Abbie Brown is among 10 Loughborough Lightning re-signings ahead of the 2026/27 edition of JAECOO Premiership Women's Rugby.
Rugby.body:
GB Sevens captain Abbie Brown is among 10 Loughborough Lightning re-signings ahead of the 2026/27 edition of JAECOO Premiership Women’s Rugby. Brown, 30, is the second longest serving member of Nathan Smith’s squad at cinch Stadium at Franklin’s Gardens, although she has only made 15 appearances in African Violet since her October 2020 arrival.

She was selected for the 2016 and 2020 Olympic Games, but missed out on 2024 selection with a hamstring injury. Last season Brown had initially intended to step away from elite rugby sevens but ultimately made her Great Britain return at the HSBC SVNS Series and at all three HSBC SVNS World Championship events.

Rugby.title: Ex-Japan coach Dan Bowden returns to the UK with URC outfit
Rugby.summary: Nearly 10 years since he hung up his playing boots and left Bath, Dan Bowden has returned to the UK as an assistant coach with Cardiff Rugby.
Rugby.body:
Nearly 10 years since he hung up his playing boots and left Bath, Dan Bowden has returned to the UK as an assistant coach with Cardiff Rugby. The former New Zealand age-grade fly-half also had spells at London Irish and Leicester in the Prem, having made a name for himself as a gifted playmaker in Super Rugby with the Highlanders.

On retiring from playing, Bowden initially took up a talent identification and recruitment manager role at Auckland, before moving into coaching. Bowden, 40, helped the capital city club to the NPC title in 2018 and won more silverware in two seasons with Toshiba Brave Lupus in Japan, as they secured back-to-back League One titles, before joining Eddie Jones in the national set-up in 2024.

Rugby.title: Did Scotland show Dave Rennie's All Blacks how to beat the Boks?
Rugby.summary: South Africa didn’t lose but the way Scotland breached their defence has given the New Zealand coach an invaluable template for their 'Greatest Rivalry' series.
Rugby.body:
Springbok Svengali Rassie Erasmus is the best card counter at the black-jack table in the history of professional rugby, bar none, and most of the risks he takes on are carefully weighted to succeed. He plays the hand he is dealt deftly, every card flipped over revealing new information and changing the way he bets on the future. The Nations Championship match against Scotland at Loftus Versveld on Saturday afternoon represented one of his rare miscalculations, and it may yet come back to bite him in ‘The Greatest Rivalry’ tour which kicks off in just over three weeks’ time.

Rassie’s selections in the first two rounds of the new competition predicted that England would present a more formidable challenge than Scotland. He picked a full-strength matchday squad to take on Steve Borthwick’s charges but selected at least eight players who would typically be outside the top South African 23 in his starting XV to play Gregor Townsend’s men.

Rugby.body:
The final week of the July series of the Nations Championship and Nations Cup is upon us, and with it, the last chance until November to see sides around the world do battle in this new tournament.

Rugby.title: Reds name settled side for semi-final after famous win over fierce rivals
Rugby.summary: The Queensland Reds will field an unchanged starting side for a Super Rugby Women’s semi-final against the Fijian Drua in Lautoka.
Rugby.body:
The Queensland Reds will field an unchanged starting side for a Super Rugby Women’s semi-final against the Fijian Drua in Lautoka, with the inclusion of Wests hooker Mary Tuaana on the bench the sole change to the matchday 23.

Queensland secured a first-ever win over fierce rivals the NSW Waratahs in the final round of the regular season, but another tough challenge looms. The Reds are just days away from a knockout match against the Drua, who finished in first place on the ladder.

Rugby.title: Wallaroos winger, SVNS star headline Waratahs side for semi-final
Rugby.summary: Wallaroos winger Maya Stewart will wear the cambridge blue jersey of the NSW Waratahs for the first time this season on Saturday.
Rugby.body:
Wallaroos winger Maya Stewart will wear the cambridge blue jersey of the NSW Waratahs for the first time this season on Saturday, named in the run-on side for a Super Rugby Women’s semi-final against the Western Force.

Stewart was kept on the sidelines throughout the regular season because of an ankle injury but is back for finals football, as one of three changes to the starting side that was beaten by the Queensland Reds 26-19 in Sydney.

Rugby.title: From Niue to new Wales cap
Rugby.summary: Kane James' first Wales cap is rooted in a family story that stretches from Pembrokeshire to the tiny Pacific island of Niue.
Rugby.body:
Kane James' first Wales cap is rooted in a family story that stretches from Pembrokeshire to the tiny island of Niue in the Pacific Ocean. There are fewer than 2,000 people on the island, one of the world's most isolated communities.

More than 1,500 miles of ocean separate it from New Zealand, with just a single flight a week reaching its shores. Few places seem further removed from Welsh rugby, yet it is impossible to tell the story of Wales' newest international without starting there.

Rugby.body:
All Blacks assistant coach Mike Blair believes Cam Roigard’s form is right up there with the best halfbacks in the world, with the No. 9 scoring three tries in Nations Championship appearances against France and Italy.

Roigard helped the Hurricanes secure a drought-breaking Super Rugby Pacific title last month before returning to the international arena, linking up with Ruben Love in the halves in the first two matches of the season.

Rugby.title: All Blacks-Ireland rivalry peaked in 2023, it's over now
Rugby.summary: Ireland are walking into the Lions' den with poor form and an old team. The rest of the world is still doubting the All Blacks, writing off the win against Italy as a 'weak' opponent
Rugby.body:
Since the infamous breakthrough win in Chicago in 2016 for Ireland over the All Blacks, an explosive new rivalry was built between a historic power and new age challenger. New Zealand refused to accept that the plucky Irish were equals, but the string of counterpunch victories undeniably defied those beliefs. The two engaged in a tit-for-tat ledger, with Ireland logging wins in 2018, 2021, and the famous series win in New Zealand in 2022.

Throughout this time Ireland had reached the world number one ranking, challenging New Zealand’s long-standing supremacy in the game. But since the 2023 Rugby World Cup quarter-final, this shortly lived great rivalry has retreated.

It’s the latest milestone in Grandidier-Nkanang’s remarkable professional career to date, which has included Olympic gold and World Rugby recognition. In a team of Six Nations champions, the 26-year-old looked right at home in the Test arena.

Rugby.body:
Ben Donaldson feels he’s on track to face Italy with the injured Wallabies playmaker aiming to make a Test return in Perth. Donaldson and fellow flyhalf Carter Gordon both missed Australia’s Nations Championship clash with France due to calf injuries, the pair watching on in Brisbane as Australia suffered a second-half collapse to fall 42-26.

Rugby.title: 'Ireland provide the perfect means to understand what Rennie’s All Blacks need to fix before the World Cup.'
Rugby.summary: Ireland have become a respected opponent of the All Blacks in the last decade and Saturday's Test provides a yardstick of progress made
Rugby.body:
Whether it was deliberate or simply a quirk of fate, the All Blacks have been handed a playing schedule in 2026 that has remarkable similarity to then one they faced in 2022 – the one that shifted the tectonic plates underpinning New Zealand rugby.

The five-game stretch four years ago that saw the All Blacks play a three-Test home series against Ireland and then back-to-back Rugby Championship fixtures in South Africa, had deep and lasting implications. It shook the game in New Zealand and in all honesty, the ground is still trembling.

Rugby.title: Joe Hawkins: 'I'm definitely better at 12 than I am 10, but I’m happy jumping between both roles.'
Rugby.summary: After leaving Wales to experience the Gallagher Prem with Exeter Chiefs, the Scarlets playmaker has no regrets about leaving home
Rugby.body:
A handful of Welsh players are finishing up their kicking session beneath a crisp winter sky, the tops of the Andes visible above the stands of the Estadio del Bicentenario in San Juan. One of them is Joe Hawkins, who finds time to crack a couple of jokes with his teammates between shots at goal. Our conversation, which begins at the side of the pitch, has to move indoors when the stadium speakers crackle into life with the opening bars of Hen Wlad Fy Nhadau. For Hawkins, who spent two years watching Wales from afar after his move to Exeter, it is a reminder of why he came home.

Few recent transfers have sparked more debate than Hawkins’ decision to leave the Ospreys for Exeter in 2023. One of the country’s brightest young talents accepted that the move would make him unavailable for international selection, just months before the Rugby World Cup. San Juan is nearly 7,000 miles from Wales, yet it was the 160-mile journey from Swansea to Exeter that forced Hawkins to spend two years watching these occasions from afar.

Rugby.title: Scotland braced for Fiji backlash after learning lessons in Pretoria
Rugby.summary: Scotland have had enough of praise without results, says forwards coach John Dalziel, as they prepare for a Fiji backlash at Murrayfield.
Rugby.body:
In the wake of South Africa's win over Scotland in Pretoria on Saturday, head coach Rassie Erasmus, in full tummy-tickling mode, praised the visitors to the hilt, listing their big wins against Argentina, France and England this year before calling them the third best team in the world.

Kind words, but nonsense, of course. Scotland were terrific for large parts in Pretoria, but they lost. And, as Scotland forwards coach John Dalziel said on Tuesday, such praise isn't really worth a damn to them anymore, not unless it comes with the breakthrough victories they now desperately crave.

Rugby.title: £50,000 raised as Newport hosts British Rugby Sevens
Rugby.summary: £50,000 raised as Newport hosts British Rugby Sevens Shropshire Star
Rugby.body:
More than £50,000 was raised for charity as Newport hosted the British Rugby Sevens. The event on June 25 was hosted by Newport Rugby Club and welcomed more than 700 guests. Now in its third year, British Rugby Sevens has grown into one of the UK's leading business rugby events, bringing together companies, the local community and some of the country's top sevens talent for a day combining elite sport, fundraising and camaraderie among the local business community.

On the pitch, the British Army Rugby Sevens reclaimed the winning title, having previously won the tournament in 2024, in what organisers described as a fast-paced and closely fought competition despite the soaring temperatures.

Rugby.title: Key takeaways from the USA Women's Eagles and Springbok Women's two-game series
Rugby.summary: The two game series between the USA Women's Eagles and the Springbok Women ended on Saturday as a stalemate.
Rugby.body:
The two game series between the USA Women’s Eagles and the Springbok Women ended on Saturday as a stalemate. It was the first time the USA have played on South African soil, began with the Springbok Women leaving the USA stunned at Ellis Park 34-21 after leading 29-0 at halftime. The following weekend in Pretoria, the Eagles fought to win 26-19.

Sandwiched between the end of club season and in preparation for the WXV Global Series, this series offered both teams the opportunity to build momentum. For USA head coach Jack Hanratty, it provided the chance to make a statement after taking over the team in January and picked up one win at the 2026 Pacific Four Series.

England face the Pumas on Saturday at Estadio Unico Madre de Ciudades, 600 miles north west of the country's capital Buenos Aires. Argentina have played twice at the 30,000-capacity stadium - which was opened in 2021 - and have won both matches, against Scotland and South Africa.

Rugby.title: Has Ilona Maher hinted that her return to rugby is around the corner?
Rugby.summary: The USA's Ilona Maher has hinted that her return to rugby could be just around the corner on social media.
Rugby.body:
The USA’s Ilona Maher has hinted that her return to rugby could be just around the corner on social media. Last week the 29-year-old posted a selfie of herself wearing a USA Rugby t-shirt to her Instagram account that has 5.6 million followers. Behind Maher two pairs of rugby boots can be seen and the post has got tongues wagging about her future on a rugby field.

This included comments from Australia’s Maddison Levi, along with former USA teammates Nicole Heavirland and Lauren Doyle, with the latter writing “Sheeeeeeee’s baaaaaack”. Maher has not been seen on a rugby pitch since the USA Women’s Eagles exited Women’s Rugby World Cup 2025 at the group stage.

Chief executive Lance Bradley is leaving Ospreys after two and a half years with the region. The 61-year-old joined the Swansea-based side from Gloucester in January 2024 and has overseen the club during a turbulent time in Welsh rugby.

Rugby.summary: England Under-20 flanker Seb Kelly is sent off for a headbutt as his team's hopes of regaining the age-grade world title ended in semi-final defeat.
Rugby.body:
England Under-20 flanker Seb Kelly was sent off for a headbutt as his team's hopes of regaining the age-grade world title ended in semi-final defeat in Tbilisi, Georgia. England had made a strong start against defending champions South Africa, with prop Ollie Streeter and fly-half Hugh Shields' tries contributing to a 17-7 lead, when Kelly lunged at Luan Giliomee on the floor after the whistle, butting the 'Baby Boks'' full-back in the face.

Referee Kevin Bralley reviewed the incident on the advice of his television match official and issued a straight red card, reducing England to 14 players for the rest of the game.

Rugby.body:
Rob Baloucoune and Jeremy Loughman are both in contention for Ireland’s Test against New Zealand this weekend as a fully-fit squad trained on Tuesday. Baloucoune had been picked to face Australia in Sydney in the opening match of this tour but pulled out with a hamstring problem which also forced him out of the win over Japan.

Loughman, meanwhile, suffered a head injury against the Wallabies which sidelined him against Japan. But both were involved as the players trained at Kings College in Auckland ahead of this weekend’s clash at Eden Park, a venue where New Zealand are unbeaten in their last 52 games.

Rugby.title: Boks' rivals hailed as 'the team to beat at next year's World Cup' by 2007 winner
Rugby.summary: South African World Cup winner Victor Matfield has claimed only three teams can win the World Cup next year – the Springboks, the All Blacks or France.
Rugby.body:
South African World Cup winner Victor Matfield has claimed only three teams can win the World Cup next year – the Springboks, the All Blacks or France. The former Springboks lock made the claim on his Rugby Rivals podcast following the latest round of Nations Championship rugby, where all three teams came out victorious.

While the All Blacks were expected to beat Italy, as were the Boks against a Scotland side that have never won against the hosts on South African soil, France’s contest against Australia was harder to call. Fabien Galthie’s side overturned a 21-12 deficit at half-time in Brisbane to come away 26-42 victors, with Matthieu Jalibert starring at full-back.
